w: Several students residing at the Sanstha’s hostel complex in Dhuliya had come for Swamishri’s blessings at the Mandir in Mumbai. Swamishri addressed them, "Do five rosaries and remember God everyday. Study properly and when you grow up serve the country and your parents. You are students, so you should not have any addictions whatsoever. You should not eat outside food either. Since you are staying at our hostel complex you should aim to study the best and together with this do Satsang. Make your life's foundation of strong and proper. Right now you should keep only two things in mind - to study well and to do Satsang. After you graduate then you will be happier, you’ll earn money. Study now and get ready and later you won’t have to worry. If you enjoy now then you will suffer later, but if you put up with hard work and suffering while studying now, then afterwards you will have happiness, happiness and happiness."
Look at others with good feelings and be of help to them and offer devotion to God; then God will be happy, happy and happy!
We should do what pleases God. He likes one who offers devotion, one who has pure feelings and divinity for Satsang.
Through self-introspection and realisation of knowledge one experiences inner peace and happiness.

By wilfully enquiring about another’s fault you are only dumping garbage in yourself. It will pain in your stomach, you’ll get sick and experience troubles... Where is the need for you to know? God will see to that.

Along with the new pinnacled mandir coming up in Sankari through the inspiration of Swamishri several new facilities have been provided by the Sanstha. This morning Swamishri performed the ground-breaking ceremony for a new water storage tank on the mandir grounds that will provide water to the entire village of Sankari.
Swamishri performed the bhumi pujan ritual for a large assembly hall, kitchen and residential facilities on the mandir grounds.
In the evening assembly Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was honored.

Grand welcome assembly A grand welcome assembly was arranged at Hofstra University Arena in the late afternoon. Swamishri arrived at the arena at 5.55 pm. Over 150 dignitaries welcomed Swamishri in a special assembly. Thereafter several dignitaries addressed the assembly.

Thomas Souzzi, Executive, Nassau County (NY), said, “So I want His Divine Holiness to know that the people who are here before you are people who have contributed greatly to our society and continue to spread the culture that they have learned in their native country to their children, and in doing so make this country a greater country. I had a chance to read a few things about His Divine Holiness before I got here today, and one of the great lessons that I saw is because of his generosity and because of his giving and because of his humility, that he empties himself until the point where he is nothing. But it is only by recognizing that we are nothing that we can be everything and be one with each other. I hereby present this citation to His Divine Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj in fitting recognition and heartfelt appreciation of his services towards harmonious relations and the advancement of international peace.” Vijay Nambiar, Indian Ambassador to the United Nations, opined, “The ‘sarva dharma sambhav’ which we talk about in India is best represented in the Swaminarayan community itself. And it is therefore for me a great privilege to be able to be present here along with all of you to have the darshan of Pramukh Swamiji.”

New York State Senator, Michael Balboni, praised Swamishri’s precedental step of retaining peace during the terrorist attack on Akshardham. He said, “I am very involved with the issue of terrorism. That is the work that I do as chairman of Homeland Security for the state, and I’m very involved with the United States government. And it’s one thing that I’ve learned to talk about peace and acceptance. It is another to do the work of God. And when the temple was attacked, Swami took the strong position – the hard position – of bringing peace, not violence; of stopping the cycle. That is the greatest gift and the greatest lesson that anyone can give this world. And it’s truly an honor and grace to be in his presence.” Congressman Gregory Meeks shared his feelings with the assembly, “It is indeed an honor and a privilege to be here today to truly meet a man of peace. Indeed, with the Swami we know with his message and His Holiness, in this time of trouble and turmoil, it is that message that will help us all share this great globe we’re currently on.”

Congressman Anthony D. Weiner narrated his experiences and thoughts of his visit to the under-construction Akshardham monument in New Delhi, “I am honored and I am privileged to meet you. I can feel the holiness in you, and, indeed, it is a true blessing to be with you this early evening.

“I am a member of Congress, and I represent perhaps one of the largest South Asian communities anywhere outside of India. But it wasn’t until January of this year that I had ever visited India. And while there were some extraordinary moments on the trip, when we visited Akshardham, to watch the construction going on, it was cold. I am not talking it was cold for India; it was cold for anywhere. It was freezing cold. But everywhere our delegation looked, there were people with smiles on their faces, beaming with pride. “It is very easy in today’s world to open up a newspaper, to turn on a television or the radio and become a little bit pessimistic about our future. We seem to focus so much on the conflicts between peoples; so much on the things that make us different from one another. No one knows that more than in New York where we focus not only on what city we’re from but we even focus on what neighborhood we’re from. But the Swami’s teachings for all of us being here today, remind us of one central fact. We all basically have the same aspirations. We want to raise our children in a better world. We want to leave a city, a community, a country, a generation just a little bit better than the one that we found. Perhaps no person is more dedicated to that than the man we have honored today. I am a Jewish boy from Brooklyn, and I am here to pay tribute to one of the finest and most godly and most wholesome people I have ever had my honor to meet.” Thomas Dinapoli, New York State Assemblyman, remarked, “I am so grateful for the beautiful blessings just bestowed upon me by this special man. We live in difficult times as we all know, and we live in times where people say there aren’t heroes for us to look up to. In Swamiji we have a hero for us all to look up to. His spirituality, his goodness, his generosity, the ways in which he uplifts in a religious and a spiritual sense is significant, but also significant are the ways in which his efforts help the medical and health needs of those who are in desperate condition.” The BAPS Care website, which highlights the Sanstha’s social activities, was inaugurated by Swamishri. Then a traditional welcome dance was performed by youths of the Boston center in honor of Swamishri.
Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly by elaborating upon the concept of destruction and true progress in our world due to materialism and spirituality respectively.
15 to 19 May Swamishri blessed the second Sant Shibir.
